html:
The Banawá are a small Indigenous people of the Banawá River in Amazonas state, Brazil, between the Juruá and Purus rivers. About 150 Banawá live in one main village and two smaller settlements. They speak a form of the Madi language of the Arawan family, the same language as the Jamamadi and Jarawara.

Like other peoples of the Purus basin they were pushed into retreat by rubber tappers during the rubber boom. They farm manioc and hunt and fish in the forest. Neighbours: Suruwahá.
